findings.title: R2-F028 systems.py:53-56 does not register probes and is invisible to the canonical auditor
findings.reproduction: R2-F028 measured_evidence says 'systems.py:53-56 registers probes' with structured line_ranges [[53,56]]. Independent source read of the frozen baseline shows register_system is AST span 46-64 and probe_system is AST span 67-88; lines 53-56 are the tail of register_system's docstring ('never fabricated. Secret-like values are refused.'), then 'capabilities = capabilities or {}' and '_reject_secrets(...)'. No probe registration occurs at 53-56; system.probe_recorded is created in probe_system at 67-88. audit_r2_spans.py only checks ranges whose start is an AST node start, so range 53-56 is skipped (one of 54 non-node-start ranges) and checked=80 mismatches=0 cannot detect it. This is the same evidence-accuracy defect class as rounds 1-4.
findings.invariant: AST-exact, semantically accurate evidence: every cited structured and prose range must correspond to a node span or a documented statement range whose content actually supports the finding claim.

findings.title: R2 event-coverage count method is undocumented and method-dependent
findings.reproduction: R2-F012 and R2_METRICS.json claim 'Source creates 113 distinct event_type values'. Independent AST/raw scans of Event.create literal first arguments in src find 112 distinct values. A deterministic partial static resolution (112 literals plus direct helper call-site literal canary.completed) reproduces exactly 113, matching the frozen metric; a fuller static resolution of helper/method call sites and defaults yields 123+, and the total is not stable across resolution rules. build_r2_evidence.py hardcodes 113 in event_coverage without a reproducible computation. The unhandled count 41 and all family counts (portfolio.* 7, connector.* 3, correlation.* 3) reproduce exactly and do not depend on this ambiguity.
findings.invariant: Reproducible evidence: every numeric claim must have a documented, script-generated counting method and exact command output.
